title: College Prep English 1 & 2 (12th)
description: College prep English - literature, composition, rhetoric

questions.question: Identify the author of 'The Great Gatsby.'
questions.explanation: F. Scott Fitzgerald published The Great Gatsby in 1925, the defining novel of the Jazz Age.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Gatsby raises a green-light toast, and Fitzgerald picks up the tab!

questions.question: Identify the author of 'The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn.'
questions.explanation: Mark Twain, the pen name of Samuel Clemens, wrote Huckleberry Finn, published in 1884.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Twain steers the raft - follow the Mississippi current to the right answer!

questions.question: Which novel features the character Atticus Finch?
questions.explanation: Atticus Finch is the principled lawyer father in Harper Lee's To Kill a Mockingbird (1960).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Atticus stands tall in the courtroom - mockingbirds sing for the innocent!

questions.question: Identify the author of the poem 'The Raven.'
questions.explanation: Edgar Allan Poe published 'The Raven' in 1845, famous for its refrain 'Nevermore.'
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Nevermore! Poe's raven croaks the author's name all night!

questions.question:
Passage: At Central City College, the vacant lot behind the library should become a student-run community garden. A garden would give students inexpensive access to fresh vegetables at a time when grocery prices near campus have risen sharply. It would also turn an unused space that now collects litter into a place where classes in biology and nutrition can conduct hands-on work. Critics worry that students lack time to maintain plots, but a similar garden at a neighboring college thrives because each plot is cared for by a team of four students who rotate weekly duties. For little cost, the college gains food, learning space, and a cleaner campus.

What is the main claim of the passage?
questions.correctAnswer: The vacant lot behind the library should become a student-run community garden.
distractors: The college should pave the vacant lot to create more parking.
Students should buy more vegetables from grocery stores near campus.
Biology and nutrition classes should stop doing hands-on work.
questions.explanation: The first sentence states the claim directly, and every later sentence gives a reason for it: cheaper food, a cleaner lot, and hands-on learning space. A main claim is the position the whole passage defends, not one supporting detail.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: find the claim in the first bite - the whole passage chews on it!

questions.question:
Passage: At Central City College, the vacant lot behind the library should become a student-run community garden. A garden would give students inexpensive access to fresh vegetables at a time when grocery prices near campus have risen sharply. It would also turn an unused space that now collects litter into a place where classes in biology and nutrition can conduct hands-on work. Critics worry that students lack time to maintain plots, but a similar garden at a neighboring college thrives because each plot is cared for by a team of four students who rotate weekly duties. For little cost, the college gains food, learning space, and a cleaner campus.

Which detail from the passage best supports the idea that the garden would help students with food costs?
questions.correctAnswer: Grocery prices near campus have risen sharply, and the garden would give students inexpensive access to fresh vegetables.
distractors: The vacant lot now collects litter.
Biology and nutrition classes could conduct hands-on work in the garden.
Each plot would be cared for by a team of four students.
questions.explanation: Only this detail connects prices and cost to food: rising grocery prices plus inexpensive vegetables. The litter detail supports a cleaner campus, the class detail supports learning, and the team detail answers a time concern - each detail supports a different point.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: match the detail to its point - cost details prove cost claims!

questions.question:
Passage: At Central City College, the vacant lot behind the library should become a student-run community garden. A garden would give students inexpensive access to fresh vegetables at a time when grocery prices near campus have risen sharply. It would also turn an unused space that now collects litter into a place where classes in biology and nutrition can conduct hands-on work. Critics worry that students lack time to maintain plots, but a similar garden at a neighboring college thrives because each plot is cared for by a team of four students who rotate weekly duties. For little cost, the college gains food, learning space, and a cleaner campus.

How does the writer respond to the concern that students lack time to maintain the garden?
questions.correctAnswer: By pointing to a neighboring college where a similar garden thrives because teams of four students rotate weekly duties.
distractors: By arguing that students have unlimited free time during the term.
By proposing that the college hire a full-time gardener to do all the work.
By admitting the concern is correct and dropping the proposal.
questions.explanation: The writer concedes the worry in one clause, then answers it with a working example: shared plots and rotating duties spread the time cost. Answering a counterargument with a real example is stronger than denying the concern exists.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: answer the worry with a working example - rotation shares the load!

questions.question:
Passage: At Central City College, the vacant lot behind the library should become a student-run community garden. A garden would give students inexpensive access to fresh vegetables at a time when grocery prices near campus have risen sharply. It would also turn an unused space that now collects litter into a place where classes in biology and nutrition can conduct hands-on work. Critics worry that students lack time to maintain plots, but a similar garden at a neighboring college thrives because each plot is cared for by a team of four students who rotate weekly duties. For little cost, the college gains food, learning space, and a cleaner campus.

What is the author's primary purpose in the passage?
questions.correctAnswer: To persuade readers that the college should turn the vacant lot into a student-run community garden.
distractors: To explain step by step how to plant and harvest vegetables.
To narrate the history of the vacant lot behind the library.
To describe how the neighboring college schedules its classes.
questions.explanation: The passage takes a position with the word 'should' and supports it with benefits while answering an objection - the marks of persuasion. It gives no planting steps, tells no history, and mentions the neighboring college only as evidence.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 'should' plus reasons means persuade - spot the stance first!

questions.question: A student writes two versions of the same request: a formal email to a professor asking for an extension, and a short casual message to a classmate asking for class notes. Which element of the rhetorical situation most directly explains why the tone and level of detail differ between the two versions?
questions.correctAnswer: the audience - each version is written for a different reader with a different relationship to the writer
distractors: the exigence - each version was prompted by a completely different problem
the citation style - each version must follow a different documentation system
the length of the course - each version covers a different number of class weeks
questions.explanation: Audience is who will read the text and what that reader expects. A professor expects formality and a clear reason; a classmate expects neither. The problem prompting both messages is the same missed work, so the exigence does not explain the difference in tone.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: change the reader, change the roar - audience shapes the tone!

questions.question: After the campus food pantry runs out of supplies twice in one month, a student writes a letter urging the student government to increase the pantry's funding. In rhetorical terms, what is the exigence of this letter?
questions.correctAnswer: The repeated pantry shortages - the problem that prompted the writer to act
distractors: The student government members who will read the letter
The writer's goal of securing more funding for the pantry
The formal tone the writer uses throughout the letter
questions.explanation: Exigence is the problem or occasion that calls the writing into being - here, the two shortages. The student government is the audience, securing funding is the purpose, and tone is a stylistic choice; naming each element separately keeps a rhetorical analysis precise.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: exigence is the itch - the problem that makes the writer write!

questions.question: Identify the author of 'Pride and Prejudice.'
questions.explanation: Jane Austen published Pride and Prejudice in 1813, featuring Elizabeth Bennet and Mr. Darcy.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Austen minds the manners - pride meets prejudice at the ball!

questions.question: Identify the author of '1984.'
questions.explanation: George Orwell published the dystopian novel 1984 in 1949, introducing Big Brother and Newspeak.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Big Brother is watching - Orwell's 1984 never blinks!

questions.question: Identify the author of 'A Tale of Two Cities.'
questions.explanation: Charles Dickens wrote A Tale of Two Cities (1859), set during the French Revolution.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: it was the best of times - Dickens doubles the cities!

questions.question: Which Romantic poet wrote 'Ode to a Nightingale'?
questions.explanation: John Keats composed 'Ode to a Nightingale' in 1819, one of his great odes.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Keats hears the nightingale - the ode sings in the dark!

questions.question: Identify the author of 'Frankenstein.'
questions.explanation: Mary Shelley wrote Frankenstein (1818) at age 18, creating the modern science-fiction novel.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Shelley's monster stomps - Mary built him from spare parts!

questions.question: Identify the author of 'Lord of the Flies.'
questions.explanation: William Golding published Lord of the Flies in 1954, about schoolboys stranded on an island.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the flies buzz on the island - Golding rules the stranded boys!

questions.question: Identify the author of 'Wuthering Heights.'
questions.explanation: Emily Bronte published Wuthering Heights in 1847 under the pen name Ellis Bell.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the winds howl on the moors - Emily's Heights never calm down!

questions.question: Determine the historical event that 'Animal Farm' allegorizes.
questions.explanation: Orwell's Animal Farm (1945) satirizes the Russian Revolution, with the pigs as Bolshevik leaders.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the pigs take the farm - Orwell's animals replay the Revolution!

questions.question: Identify the author of the Sherlock Holmes stories.
questions.explanation: Sir Arthur Conan Doyle created Sherlock Holmes, debuting in A Study in Scarlet (1887).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: elementary! Doyle's detective deduces every clue!

questions.question: Identify the author of 'Brave New World.'
questions.explanation: Aldous Huxley published the dystopian Brave New World in 1932.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Huxley's brave new world - soma keeps everyone smiling!

questions.question: Which term best describes a recurring object that represents an abstract idea?
questions.explanation: A symbol is a concrete object standing for an abstract idea, like a dove for peace.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a dove means peace - symbols wear costumes as ideas!

questions.question: Identify the term for the main character who drives the plot.
questions.explanation: The protagonist is the central character whose goals drive the story forward.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the protagonist leads the parade - follow the main dino!

questions.question: Which term best describes a character who contrasts with another to highlight traits?
questions.explanation: A foil's contrasting qualities throw the main character's traits into sharper relief.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a foil is the shiny opposite - contrast makes characters pop!

questions.question: Identify the term for the turning point of a story's plot.
questions.explanation: The climax is the moment of highest tension where the central conflict turns.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the climax is the mountain top - the plot can't climb higher!

questions.question: Which term best describes a story's time and place?
questions.explanation: Setting is the when and where of a narrative; mood is the feeling it creates.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: setting sets the stage - time and place paint the backdrop!

questions.question: Determine the term for the central message or insight of a work.
questions.explanation: Theme is the underlying message about life or human nature, distinct from plot events.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the theme is the treasure - dig under the plot to find it!

questions.question: Identify which pronouns a first-person singular narrator uses.
questions.explanation: First-person singular narration uses I/me/my (the first-person plural forms are we/us/our); second person uses you; third person uses he/she/they.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: I tell my own tale - first person keeps it personal!

questions.question: Which term best describes a comparison using 'like' or 'as'?
questions.explanation: A simile compares two things with like or as; a metaphor states the comparison directly.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: like, as - similes compare with training wheels!

questions.question: Identify the term for giving human qualities to nonhuman things.
questions.explanation: Personification attributes human traits to objects or ideas, like 'the wind whispered.'
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the wind whispers - personification gives things a voice!

questions.question: Which term best describes extreme exaggeration used for effect?
questions.explanation: Hyperbole is deliberate overstatement, as in 'I've told you a million times.'
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a million times over - hyperbole never does anything small!

questions.question: In rhetoric, determine what ethos appeals to in an audience.
questions.explanation: Ethos builds trust through the speaker's character, expertise, and credibility.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: trust the badge - ethos flashes credentials!

questions.question: In rhetoric, determine what pathos appeals to in an audience.
questions.explanation: Pathos persuades by stirring feelings such as sympathy, anger, or hope.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: pathos pulls heartstrings - feel the argument!

questions.question: In rhetoric, determine what logos appeals to in an audience.
questions.explanation: Logos relies on evidence, facts, and logical reasoning to persuade.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: logos loves logic - numbers and reasons rule!

questions.question: Identify the rhetorical device in which a speaker says the opposite of what they mean for effect.
questions.explanation: Verbal irony is a statement whose intended meaning is the opposite of its literal words.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: say the opposite with a wink - verbal irony talks backwards!

questions.question: Which term best describes dramatic irony, when the audience knows something a character does not?
questions.explanation: Dramatic irony creates tension because viewers know more than the characters on stage.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: you know, they don't - dramatic irony keeps secrets from the stage!

questions.question: Identify the rhetorical device of repeating a word or phrase at the start of successive clauses.
questions.explanation: Anaphora repeats openings, as in 'I have a dream... I have a dream' from Dr. King.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: I have a dream, I have a dream - anaphora repeats the drumbeat!

questions.question: Which term best describes a question asked for effect rather than an answer?
questions.explanation: A rhetorical question makes a point; the speaker does not expect a reply.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: who needs an answer? Rhetorical questions ask for effect!

questions.question: Identify the logical fallacy of misrepresenting an opponent's argument to attack the weaker version.
questions.explanation: A straw man distorts the other side's position into an easier target to knock down.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: don't fight a straw dino - attack the real argument!

questions.question: Identify the logical fallacy of attacking the person instead of their argument.
questions.explanation: Ad hominem means 'to the person' - it dodges the argument by insulting the arguer.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: argue the point, not the person - ad hominem misses the target!

questions.question: Determine the rhetorical device used in 'I came, I saw, I conquered.'
questions.explanation: Parallelism repeats the same grammatical structure across clauses for rhythm and force.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: march in step - parallel structure keeps clauses in formation!

questions.question: Determine where a thesis statement usually appears in an essay.
questions.correctAnswer: at the end of the introduction
distractors: at the start of the introduction
in the middle of the body
questions.explanation: Placing the thesis at the end of the introduction lets context build before the main claim lands.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the thesis lands the intro - last line, main claim!

questions.question: Which best describes a counterargument in an essay?
questions.correctAnswer: an opposing view the writer addresses
questions.explanation: Acknowledging a counterargument shows fairness and lets the writer answer objections.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: hear the other side - counterarguments steel-man the opposition!

questions.question: Determine the function of a rebuttal in an essay.
questions.correctAnswer: responds to and refutes a counterargument
questions.explanation: After raising a counterargument, the rebuttal explains why it fails or is outweighed.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: rebuttal roars back - answer the objection and move on!

questions.question: Which is the strongest thesis statement?
questions.correctAnswer: School uniforms limit student self-expression and should be optional.
questions.explanation: A strong thesis is specific and arguable; the others are vague, announcing, or factual.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a thesis takes a stand - arguable and specific wins!

questions.question: Determine the function of topic sentences in body paragraphs.
questions.correctAnswer: introduce the main idea of a paragraph
questions.explanation: Each body paragraph opens with a topic sentence that connects its point to the thesis.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: every paragraph needs a captain - the topic sentence leads!

questions.question: Determine the primary function of transitions between paragraphs.
distractors: repeat the thesis word for word
questions.explanation: Transitions signal how ideas connect - contrast, cause, sequence, or addition.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: transitions are bridges - ideas cross without falling!

questions.question: Identify what a writer should NOT do in a conclusion.
questions.explanation: New evidence belongs in the body; the conclusion synthesizes what was already argued.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the conclusion wraps the gift - no new surprises inside!

questions.question: Determine how a writer mainly builds ethos in an essay.
questions.explanation: Credible sources show the writer is informed and trustworthy, strengthening ethos.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: cite the experts - borrowed credibility boosts your ethos!

questions.question: Choose the strongest primary evidence for a literary analysis essay.
questions.explanation: Direct textual evidence grounds claims about literature better than outside commentary.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: let the text testify - quotes are your star witnesses!

questions.question: Determine the defining feature of a synthesis essay.
questions.correctAnswer: combines multiple sources into a new argument
questions.explanation: Synthesis weaves sources together so their combination produces an original claim.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: synthesis stirs the pot - blend sources into something new!

questions.question: Choose the correct verb: 'If I ___ taller, I would play basketball.'
questions.explanation: The subjunctive mood uses 'were' for wishes and hypotheticals, even with singular subjects.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: wish upon were - the subjunctive dreams in were!

questions.question: Choose the parallel option: 'She likes hiking, swimming, and ___.'
questions.explanation: Parallel structure keeps all items in the same form - three gerunds here.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: hiking, swimming, reading - keep the -ing parade uniform!

questions.question: Identify the error in 'Running quickly, the finish line approached.'
questions.correctAnswer: The modifier dangles - the finish line was not running.
questions.explanation: The participial phrase must modify the subject, but the subject here cannot run.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: who is running? Modifiers must cling to the right noun!

questions.question: Choose the correct verb: 'Neither the teacher nor the students ___ ready.'
questions.explanation: With neither/nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject - the plural 'students.'
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the verb hugs the nearer subject - students were ready!

questions.question: Choose the correct pronoun: 'Between you and ___, this test is hard.'
questions.explanation: Prepositions take object pronouns - 'between you and me' is correct.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: prepositions love objects - between you and me!

questions.question: Choose the correct word: 'The storm ended; ___, the streets were flooded.'
questions.explanation: A conjunctive adverb like 'however' follows a semicolon to join two independent clauses.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: semicolon plus however - a fancy pause with manners!

questions.question: Choose the correct verb: 'The committee ___ reached its decision.'
questions.explanation: A collective noun acting as one unit takes a singular verb.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the committee acts as one - singular group, singular verb!

questions.question: Which sentence best demonstrates the subjunctive mood?
questions.correctAnswer: I suggest that he study harder.
questions.explanation: Verbs like suggest, demand, and insist trigger the subjunctive - base form 'study,' not 'studies.'
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: suggest, demand, insist - then drop the s!

questions.question: Identify the error in 'She served sandwiches to the children on paper plates.'
questions.correctAnswer: The modifier is misplaced - the plates could describe the children.
questions.explanation: The phrase 'on paper plates' sits next to 'children,' creating unintended humor.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: park the modifier next to its noun - no wandering phrases!

questions.question: Choose the correct word: 'The new policy will ___ test scores.'
questions.explanation: 'Affect' is usually the verb meaning to influence; 'effect' is usually the noun meaning result.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: affect is the action - A for action, E for the noun effect!

questions.question:
Passage: A rain garden is a shallow, planted basin designed to collect stormwater that runs off roofs, driveways, and streets. Unlike a regular flower bed, a rain garden is dug several inches below the surrounding ground and filled with loose, sandy soil that lets water soak in quickly. Native plants with deep roots are chosen because their roots create channels that help water move downward and because the plants can tolerate both brief flooding and dry spells between rains. Within 24 to 48 hours after a storm, most of the collected water has filtered into the ground instead of flowing into storm drains. As the water passes through soil and roots, many pollutants are trapped or broken down, so less contaminated water reaches nearby streams.

According to the passage, why is a rain garden filled with loose, sandy soil?
questions.correctAnswer: So that collected water can soak into the ground quickly.
distractors: So that the basin can stay flooded for a full week after each storm.
So that storm drains near the garden can be permanently removed.
So that the native plants will never need water between rains.
questions.explanation: The passage links the soil directly to speed of absorption: loose, sandy soil 'lets water soak in quickly.' The basin is meant to drain within 24 to 48 hours, not stay flooded, and no claim is made about removing drains.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: sandy soil, speedy soak - loose grains let water slip through!

questions.question:
Passage: A rain garden is a shallow, planted basin designed to collect stormwater that runs off roofs, driveways, and streets. Unlike a regular flower bed, a rain garden is dug several inches below the surrounding ground and filled with loose, sandy soil that lets water soak in quickly. Native plants with deep roots are chosen because their roots create channels that help water move downward and because the plants can tolerate both brief flooding and dry spells between rains. Within 24 to 48 hours after a storm, most of the collected water has filtered into the ground instead of flowing into storm drains. As the water passes through soil and roots, many pollutants are trapped or broken down, so less contaminated water reaches nearby streams.

According to the passage, what do the deep roots of the native plants do to help water move?
questions.correctAnswer: They create channels that help water move downward into the ground.
distractors: They block water at the surface so it evaporates in the sun.
They push collected water sideways into the nearest storm drain.
They store all of the stormwater inside the plants for a month.
questions.explanation: The passage states the mechanism plainly: roots 'create channels that help water move downward.' The plants are also chosen because they tolerate both flooding and dry spells, but tolerance is not the water-moving mechanism asked for here.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: roots are roadways - channels carry the water down!

questions.question:
Passage: A rain garden is a shallow, planted basin designed to collect stormwater that runs off roofs, driveways, and streets. Unlike a regular flower bed, a rain garden is dug several inches below the surrounding ground and filled with loose, sandy soil that lets water soak in quickly. Native plants with deep roots are chosen because their roots create channels that help water move downward and because the plants can tolerate both brief flooding and dry spells between rains. Within 24 to 48 hours after a storm, most of the collected water has filtered into the ground instead of flowing into storm drains. As the water passes through soil and roots, many pollutants are trapped or broken down, so less contaminated water reaches nearby streams.

According to the passage, what happens to most of the water collected in a rain garden within 24 to 48 hours after a storm?
questions.correctAnswer: It has filtered into the ground instead of flowing into storm drains.
distractors: It has evaporated completely into the air above the basin.
It has been pumped into storage tanks for later use on lawns.
It is still standing in the basin at the end of the second day.
questions.explanation: The passage gives a specific time window and outcome: within 24 to 48 hours, most water 'has filtered into the ground instead of flowing into storm drains.' Filtering downward is the whole design - the basin is shallow and drains, so standing water is the exception, not the rule.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: two days, then down it goes - filtered into the ground, not the drain!

questions.question:
Passage: A rain garden is a shallow, planted basin designed to collect stormwater that runs off roofs, driveways, and streets. Unlike a regular flower bed, a rain garden is dug several inches below the surrounding ground and filled with loose, sandy soil that lets water soak in quickly. Native plants with deep roots are chosen because their roots create channels that help water move downward and because the plants can tolerate both brief flooding and dry spells between rains. Within 24 to 48 hours after a storm, most of the collected water has filtered into the ground instead of flowing into storm drains. As the water passes through soil and roots, many pollutants are trapped or broken down, so less contaminated water reaches nearby streams.

According to the passage, how do rain gardens help protect nearby streams?
questions.correctAnswer: As water passes through soil and roots, many pollutants are trapped or broken down, so less contaminated water reaches the streams.
distractors: The gardens add fertilizer to the water so stream plants grow faster.
The gardens send all stormwater to storm drains before it can reach streams.
The native plants drink every drop of water, so nothing ever leaves the garden.
questions.explanation: The benefit to streams is filtration: soil and roots trap or break down pollutants during the downward trip. Sending water to storm drains is what rain gardens reduce, and 'every drop' overstates a passage that says 'most' of the water filters in.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: soil is a filter - trapped pollutants never reach the stream!

questions.question: Speaking at a city council meeting one week after a major flood damaged homes in her neighborhood, a resident describes the damage and asks the council to fund repairs to the storm drains. What is the speaker's primary purpose in this context?
questions.correctAnswer: To persuade the council to fund storm drain repairs
distractors: To entertain the council with a personal story about the flood
To explain in detail how storm drains are engineered and built
To inform residents about the council's regular meeting schedule
questions.explanation: Purpose is what the speaker wants the audience to do or decide. The recent flood is the context that makes the request urgent, but the speech aims at a decision - funding repairs. She describes damage as evidence for that request, not as entertainment or as an engineering lesson.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: purpose is the prize - she speaks so the council will act!

questions.question: In APA style (7th edition), a student directly quotes page 14 of a 2021 journal article by Maria Johnson. Which parenthetical citation at the end of the quoted sentence is correct in APA style?
questions.explanation: APA in-text citations give the author surname, the year, and - for a direct quotation - a page locator with 'p.': (Johnson, 2021, p. 14). The form (Johnson 14) is MLA style, which omits the year; APA requires the page for quotations, so the year alone is incomplete.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: APA packs three facts - author, year, page for a quote!

questions.question: Which definition best matches 'tenuous' in the sentence: 'The link between the events was tenuous.'
questions.explanation: Tenuous describes something flimsy with little substance.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: tenuous is thin - a spider thread of a link!

questions.question: Which definition best matches 'ennui' in the sentence: 'She felt a deep ennui.'
questions.explanation: Ennui is a French-derived word for weary dissatisfaction and boredom.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: ennui is elegant boredom - a fancy yawn!

questions.question: Which definition best matches 'lugubrious' in the sentence: 'He spoke in a lugubrious tone.'
questions.explanation: Lugubrious means sorrowful to an exaggerated degree.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: lugubrious is gloomy - a funeral march in an adjective!

questions.question: Which definition best matches 'dictum' in the sentence: 'The old dictum still holds true.'
questions.explanation: A dictum is a formal pronouncement treated as authoritative.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a dictum dictates - an authority's say-so in a sentence!

questions.question: Which reference list entry follows APA style (7th edition) for a journal article?
questions.correctAnswer: Lee, D. (2020). Study habits and memory in first-year students. Journal of College Reading, 12, 45-60.
distractors: Lee, David. 2020. Study Habits and Memory in First-Year Students. Journal of College Reading, 12, 45-60.
Lee, D. (2020). Study Habits and Memory in First-Year Students. journal of college reading, 12, 45-60.
(Lee, D., 2020). Study habits and memory in first-year students. Journal of College Reading, 12, 45-60.
questions.explanation: APA reference entries use the surname plus initials, the year in parentheses right after the author, sentence case for the article title (only the first word and proper nouns capitalized), and title case for the journal name. Each wrong entry breaks at least one of those rules - a full first name, a missing parenthesis pair, or the wrong capitalization pattern.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: surname, initials, (year) - and the article title stays sentence case in APA!

questions.question: Which revision correctly fixes the comma splice in this sentence? 'The writing workshop filled quickly, students were placed on a waitlist.'
questions.correctAnswer: The writing workshop filled quickly; students were placed on a waitlist.
distractors: The writing workshop filled quickly, students were placed on a waitlist.
The writing workshop filled quickly. Students on a waitlist.
The writing workshop filled quickly, and, students were placed on a waitlist.
questions.explanation: A comma splice joins two independent clauses with only a comma. A semicolon can join two closely related independent clauses on its own, which fixes the splice here. The second option repeats the splice, the third leaves a fragment ('Students on a waitlist' has no verb), and the fourth strands 'and' between commas.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: two full clauses need more than a comma - the semicolon is the stronger bridge!

questions.question: Determine how many syllables a line of iambic pentameter contains.
questions.explanation: Penta means five - five iambic feet of two syllables each equals ten syllables.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: five heartbeats per line - ten syllables march in pentameter!

questions.question: Identify the metrical foot of an unstressed syllable followed by a stressed syllable.
questions.explanation: The iamb (da-DUM) is the most common foot in English verse.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: da-DUM, da-DUM - the iamb hops like a heartbeat!

questions.question: Which term best describes a poem mourning the dead?
questions.explanation: An elegy is a formal lament for someone who has died.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: an elegy weeps in verse - mourning set to meter!

questions.question: Determine the meaning of enjambment in poetry.
questions.correctAnswer: a sentence running past a line break without punctuation
distractors: a rhyme at the ends of lines
a pause in the middle of a line
questions.explanation: Enjambment carries the sense over the line ending, pulling the reader forward.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: enjambment jumps the line - the sentence leaps the break!

questions.question: In Carl Sandburg's 'Fog,' determine the figurative device in the line 'comes on little cat feet.'
questions.explanation: The fog is directly compared to a cat without like or as, making it a metaphor.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: fog on cat feet - Sandburg's metaphor pads in silently!

questions.question: In Frost's 'The Road Not Taken,' determine what the two roads most likely symbolize.
questions.explanation: The forked roads are a classic symbol for decisions that shape a life.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: two roads diverged - Frost's fork is life's choices!

questions.question: Determine how many syllables a traditional haiku contains.
questions.explanation: Haiku follow a 5-7-5 syllable pattern across three lines, totaling 17.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: five-seven-five, seventeen - haiku counts on its fingers!

questions.question: Which statement best describes the defining feature of free verse?
questions.explanation: Free verse abandons fixed patterns, using natural speech rhythms instead.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: free verse runs wild - no rhyme, no meter, no cage!

questions.question:
Passage: On my first night volunteering at the campus observatory, I arrived certain I would impress everyone with the astronomy terms I had memorized. Instead, when a young visitor asked why the Moon looked larger near the horizon, I froze. Dr. Alvarez, the astronomer in charge, did not answer for me. She handed the girl a small ball and a flashlight and said, 'Show us what you think happens.' As the girl moved the ball around the light, I realized I had been preparing to perform knowledge rather than help someone discover it. For the rest of the evening, I listened more than I spoke, asking visitors what they noticed before I offered any explanation. I left with fewer facts delivered, but I had finally begun to learn how to teach.

What realization does the narrator reach as the girl moves the ball around the flashlight?
questions.correctAnswer: She had been preparing to perform her knowledge rather than help someone else discover an idea.
distractors: The astronomy terms she had memorized turned out to be incorrect.
Dr. Alvarez was disappointed in her and would not invite her back.
Young visitors learn best from a lecture with many technical terms.
questions.explanation: The narrator states the realization in her own words: she had prepared 'to perform knowledge rather than help someone discover it.' Nothing in the passage says her terms were wrong or that Dr. Alvarez was disappointed - the tone is reflective, not punished.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: performing is not teaching - discovery beats showing off!

questions.question:
Passage: On my first night volunteering at the campus observatory, I arrived certain I would impress everyone with the astronomy terms I had memorized. Instead, when a young visitor asked why the Moon looked larger near the horizon, I froze. Dr. Alvarez, the astronomer in charge, did not answer for me. She handed the girl a small ball and a flashlight and said, 'Show us what you think happens.' As the girl moved the ball around the light, I realized I had been preparing to perform knowledge rather than help someone discover it. For the rest of the evening, I listened more than I spoke, asking visitors what they noticed before I offered any explanation. I left with fewer facts delivered, but I had finally begun to learn how to teach.

Why does Dr. Alvarez hand the girl a ball and a flashlight instead of answering her question directly?
questions.correctAnswer: To invite the girl to explore her own thinking about the question.
distractors: Because she does not know why the Moon looks larger near the horizon.
To test whether the narrator has memorized enough astronomy terms.
Because the observatory has a rule against speaking to young visitors.
questions.explanation: Her instruction - 'Show us what you think happens' - turns the question back into an experiment the girl can run herself. That models the discovery-based teaching the narrator then imitates for the rest of the evening by asking visitors what they noticed first.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: hand over the tools, not the answer - let the learner show her thinking!

questions.question:
Passage: On my first night volunteering at the campus observatory, I arrived certain I would impress everyone with the astronomy terms I had memorized. Instead, when a young visitor asked why the Moon looked larger near the horizon, I froze. Dr. Alvarez, the astronomer in charge, did not answer for me. She handed the girl a small ball and a flashlight and said, 'Show us what you think happens.' As the girl moved the ball around the light, I realized I had been preparing to perform knowledge rather than help someone discover it. For the rest of the evening, I listened more than I spoke, asking visitors what they noticed before I offered any explanation. I left with fewer facts delivered, but I had finally begun to learn how to teach.

How does the narrator's behavior change over the course of the evening?
questions.correctAnswer: She listens more than she speaks, asking visitors what they noticed before offering any explanation.
distractors: She memorizes more astronomy terms so she can answer faster.
She stops talking to visitors and lets Dr. Alvarez handle every question.
She delivers longer lectures so visitors leave with more facts.
questions.explanation: The change is stated directly: 'I listened more than I spoke, asking visitors what they noticed before I offered any explanation.' She still teaches - the order changes. Listening comes first and explanation second, the reverse of her memorize-and-perform plan.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: listen first, explain second - the order is the lesson!

questions.question:
Passage: On my first night volunteering at the campus observatory, I arrived certain I would impress everyone with the astronomy terms I had memorized. Instead, when a young visitor asked why the Moon looked larger near the horizon, I froze. Dr. Alvarez, the astronomer in charge, did not answer for me. She handed the girl a small ball and a flashlight and said, 'Show us what you think happens.' As the girl moved the ball around the light, I realized I had been preparing to perform knowledge rather than help someone discover it. For the rest of the evening, I listened more than I spoke, asking visitors what they noticed before I offered any explanation. I left with fewer facts delivered, but I had finally begun to learn how to teach.

Which statement best expresses the central lesson of the passage?
questions.correctAnswer: Good teaching begins with listening to learners instead of showing off what you know.
distractors: Volunteering at an observatory is a waste of time for new students.
The Moon looks larger near the horizon because of the ball-and-flashlight model.
Memorizing technical terms is the best preparation for answering questions.
questions.explanation: The closing line resolves the arc: she delivered fewer facts but 'had finally begun to learn how to teach.' The passage never explains the Moon illusion itself, and her opening memorize-and-perform approach is exactly what the evening teaches her to abandon.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: fewer facts, better teaching - listening is the real telescope!

questions.question: A teacher displays projects made by several students. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence for the display sign.
questions.correctAnswer: The students' projects were displayed in the main hall.
distractors: The student's projects were displayed in the main hall.
The students projects were displayed in the main hall.
The students's projects were displayed in the main hall.
questions.explanation: When a plural noun ending in s shows possession, the apostrophe goes after the s: students' projects. 'Student's' would mean the projects of one student, which contradicts the several students in the prompt, and 'students's' is never a correct form in edited American English.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: many students, apostrophe after the s - students' shows them all!

questions.question: Choose the correct verb to complete the sentence: 'The set of revised drafts from the workshop ___ ready for review today.'
questions.explanation: The subject is 'set,' a singular noun; the phrase 'of revised drafts' sits between the subject and the verb but does not change its number. The word 'today' anchors the sentence in the present, so the singular present form 'is' is the only choice that agrees in both number and tense.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: hunt the head noun - the set is one, so the verb is 'is'!

questions.question: Identify the city where the Globe Theatre, home to Shakespeare's company, was located.
questions.explanation: The Globe stood on the south bank of the Thames in London from 1599.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: the Globe glows in London - groundlings stand for the show!

questions.question: Identify the villain who drives the plot of 'Othello.'
questions.explanation: Iago's scheming destroys Othello through jealousy and manipulation.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Iago whispers poison - Othello's villain smiles while he schemes!

questions.question: Determine how a Shakespearean tragedy typically ends.
questions.explanation: Tragedy follows the hero's fatal flaw to a catastrophic, usually fatal, close.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: tragedies fall hard - the hero falls with the curtain!

questions.question: Identify the play in which 'Beware the Ides of March' is spoken.
questions.explanation: The soothsayer warns Caesar in Act 1 of Julius Caesar.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: beware the Ides - Caesar should have checked the calendar!

questions.question: In MLA style, determine the correct format of an in-text citation for a book by one author.
questions.explanation: MLA uses author last name and page number with no comma: (Smith 42).
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: name and page in parentheses - MLA keeps it lean: (Smith 42)!

questions.question: Determine what an MLA Works Cited page lists.
questions.correctAnswer: every source cited in the paper
questions.explanation: Works Cited includes exactly the sources referenced in-text - no more, no fewer.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: cited means listed - if it's in the paper, it's on the page!

questions.question: Which of the following best describes plagiarism?
questions.explanation: Ideas need attribution even when restated; citations and common knowledge are safe.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: credit every borrow - uncredited ideas are stolen snacks!

questions.question: Choose the best example of a primary source for a history research paper.
questions.correctAnswer: A diary written during the time period
questions.explanation: Primary sources are firsthand accounts from the era; the others interpret them.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: primary means firsthand - a diary from the day beats a textbook!

questions.question: Choose the best thesis for a research paper.
questions.explanation: A research thesis makes a debatable claim narrow enough to prove with evidence.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: a thesis with teeth - specific, arguable, ready to defend!

questions.question: In MLA Works Cited, determine what a 'hanging indent' means.
questions.correctAnswer: first line flush left, remaining lines indented
questions.explanation: The hanging indent makes authors' names easy to scan down the left margin.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: first line out, rest in - the hanging indent dangles!

questions.question: Determine what you must do when you paraphrase a source.
distractors: do nothing - they are your words now
questions.explanation: Paraphrases restate ideas, but the ideas still belong to the source - cite them.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: new words, same debt - paraphrases need citations too!

questions.question: Choose the source most likely credible for academic research.
questions.explanation: Peer review means experts vetted the work before publication.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: peers check the work - journals earn the trust badge!

questions.question: Determine the purpose of an annotated bibliography.
questions.explanation: Each annotation briefly describes the source and judges its usefulness.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: annotate means assess - summarize and judge each source!

questions.question: Determine what synthesis means in research writing.
questions.correctAnswer: combining sources to form a new insight
questions.explanation: Synthesis goes beyond summary - sources interact to support an original claim.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: synthesis is alchemy - blend sources into gold!
